queue.claim: Smartphone photos (ultra-wide 'face distortion correction', front-camera beauty modes, lens correction) warp faces away from a pinhole projection, so the engine must down-weight or exclude faces near the frame edge in wide shots (f35 ≤ 16 mm, or beyond ~60% of the half-diagonal).
queue.query: smartphone ultra-wide face distortion correction warps faces near edge lens correction Pixel Samsung iPhone

queue.claim: Selfie perspective at about 0.3 m enlarges the nose markedly versus about 1.5 m (Ward et al. 2018 reported roughly 30% nasal-base widening). The engine uses this to set selfie σ multiplier 3 / exclude and a focal prior of 26 mm with σ_log 0.1.
queue.query: Ward 2018 JAMA Facial Plastic Surgery selfies nasal dimensions distance 12 inches 5 feet

queue.claim: Event and press photos of public figures are typically shot at 3–10 m with 70–300 mm full-frame-equivalent lenses (near-orthographic). This gives the focal prior median 135 mm, σ_log 0.5.
queue.query: red carpet press photographer typical lens 70-200mm shooting distance

queue.claim: Magazine covers and studio portraits are commonly retouched with liquify (jaw slimmed, eyes enlarged, neck lengthened), justifying a 2–3× σ multiplier or exclusion from proportion terms.
queue.query: magazine photo retouching liquify face shape jaw eyes prevalence study
